lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: laundry cycles and labels

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic laundry cycles and labels task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner gathers a real load of laundry, reads the care label sewn into each garment, groups the garments by color and by the most restrictive temperature or drying instruction in the group, and washes and dries that load on a household washer and dryer using the settings the labels call for.
safetyNotes: Never overload the washer or dryer past the fill line shown inside the drum; an overloaded load will not get clean or dry and can strain the machine.
Read every care label before adding any stain-treatment product to a load, since bleach-based and oxygen-based treatments react differently depending on the fabric and dye.

simulationAlternative.description: If no washer or dryer is available in the household, the learner instead reads the care labels on five real garments, records the exact wash temperature, dryer setting, and any special symbol, such as do-not-bleach, dry-flat, or low-iron, shown on each, and explains in writing what wash and dry settings would be chosen for each garment and why, without running a machine.

materials: adult-or-local: at least three real garments with attached care labels
adult-or-local: a real load of laundry
adult-or-local: access to a household washer and dryer, or the garments alone if no machine is available
adult-or-local: laundry detergent already in the household

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one garment in this load that would have been washed or dried incorrectly if you had not checked its label, and what could have gone wrong.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Label interpretation accuracy: Temperature, dryer, bleach, and iron symbols are correctly read on at least three garments and used to group the load. | Safe, correctly-set real load: Wash and dry settings match the most restrictive label in the load, and the load stays within the machine's fill line. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner find one garment with a symbol they cannot identify, look up what that symbol means, and add it to a personal reference list of care-label symbols.

resources.title: laundry cycles and labels worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner gathers a real load of laundry, reads the care label sewn into each garment, groups the garments by color and by the most restrictive temperature or drying instruction in the group, and washes and dries that load on a household washer and dryer using the settings the labels call for.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact laundry cycles and labels decision or action.
Model move 2: Read the care label inside three different garments before sorting anything.
Model move 3: Sort a real load of laundry into groups by color and by the most restrictive temperature or drying instruction found on any label in that group.

Model check: Label interpretation accuracy: Temperature, dryer, bleach, and iron symbols are correctly read on at least three garments and used to group the load. | Safe, correctly-set real load: Wash and dry settings match the most restrictive label in the load, and the load stays within the machine's fill line.

resources.title: laundry cycles and labels action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for laundry cycles and labels.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: laundry cycles and labels coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner gathers a real load of laundry, reads the care label sewn into each garment, groups the garments by color and by the most restrictive temperature or drying instruction in the group, and washes and dries that load on a household washer and dryer using the settings the labels call for.
Coach direction: Read the care label inside three different garments before sorting anything.

Learner prompt: For each of the three garments, write the water-temperature symbol and one other symbol you found, such as bleach, dryer, or iron, and name one symbol you had not noticed on a label before.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: laundry cycles and labels complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Sort a real load of laundry into groups by color and by the most restrictive temperature or drying instruction found on any label in that group.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I grouped the garments by color first, then checked every label in each color group for the lowest temperature or gentlest instruction.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I set aside any garment whose label instructions did not match the rest of its color group.

Equal-access rule: If no washer or dryer is available in the household, the learner instead reads the care labels on five real garments, records the exact wash temperature, dryer setting, and any special symbol, such as do-not-bleach, dry-flat, or low-iron, shown on each, and explains in writing what wash and dry settings would be chosen for each garment and why, without running a machine.

resources.title: laundry cycles and labels minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one garment in this load that would have been washed or dried incorrectly if you had not checked its label, and what could have gone wrong.

Success checks: Label interpretation accuracy: Temperature, dryer, bleach, and iron symbols are correctly read on at least three garments and used to group the load. | Safe, correctly-set real load: Wash and dry settings match the most restrictive label in the load, and the load stays within the machine's fill line.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: laundry cycles and labels supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional laundry cycles and labels condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Label interpretation accuracy: Temperature, dryer, bleach, and iron symbols are correctly read on at least three garments and used to group the load. | Safe, correctly-set real load: Wash and dry settings match the most restrictive label in the load, and the load stays within the machine's fill line..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
